name: Amako
confidence_why: The only phonological description of Amako (Korak), an undated SIL organised-phonology sheet based on two weeks of work, says of stress only "Stress is not phonemic?", and Z'graggen (1971, 1980) and Pick (2020) record nothing about Amako stress, so neither the placement nor the type of the stress system can be stated.

CVC kud 'banana' wal.wal 'butterfly' i.dem.suk 'to work' u.dud 'midday' [p. 1:] Organised Phonology Data / Amako Language / Madang – Madang Province / Population census: 500 / Major villages: Korak / Linguistic work done by: SIL (based on 2 weeks work) / Data checked by: [p. 2:] Long vowels /ɑː/ and /eː/ (possibly also others) [p. 3, Conventions: Orthographic:] Vowels seem to be short and long. Test using a double vowel to represent length. This orthography convention is used in a neighboring language, Mauwake, although it is not a related language.

new_statements.rule_in_words: The only first-hand source tentatively states (with a question mark) that stress is not contrastive in Amako/Korak; it does not say on which syllable stress falls, and no example word carries a stress mark. Position of word stress is therefore undescribed.
new_statements.exceptions: none; the statement itself is hedged with '?'. The same sheet notes long vowels /a:/ and /e:/ ('Vowels seem to be short and long').
new_statements.domain_note: Isolated citation words from an alphabet-development worksheet; no phrase-level data ('Transcription of a recorded passage' section is empty).
new_statements.identity_note: The only phonology sheet is titled 'Amako Language' (major village Korak; SIL archive subject language Korak [koz]); Amako is the endonym Pick 2020 adopts for Z'graggen's 'Korak' (E4). Same languoid, kora1296. Sister language Waskia (wask1241) has separate SIL phonology materials (Barker & Lee) that must not be transferred to Korak.
